mainTopic: Renting a bathhouse or a field to a גוי or a כותי: when onlookers will suspect the Jewish owner of having forbidden work done on שבת, יום טוב, or חול המועד.
overview: The גמרא first finishes the earlier point: the unnamed ruling in the משנה about renting houses follows רבי מאיר, because רבי יוסי allows renting houses everywhere. Then it quotes the next line of the משנה, which says a person may never rent out his bathhouse to a גוי. A ברייתא from רבן שמעון בן גמליאל explains why. The bathhouse is known by the owner's name, so when the גוי runs it on שבת and יום טוב, people will think the Jew is having it done. Renting to a כותי is allowed, because he would only work on חול המועד, when Jews run bathhouses too. Renting a field to a גוי is also allowed, because everyone knows a sharecropper works for his own share, while nobody sharecrops a bathhouse. Next, a ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר forbids renting a field to a כותי, since he will work it on חול המועד. The גמרא infers that a גוי is allowed because of the sharecropper reasoning, and then asks why the same reasoning does not allow a כותי too. The answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: The unnamed ruling follows רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the anonymous ruling in the משנה about not renting houses follows רבי מאיר, because רבי יוסי allows renting houses everywhere.
steps.simpleTranslation: The unnamed ruling in the משנה is like רבי מאיר. If it were רבי יוסי, he lets people rent out houses in every place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the earlier discussion by deciding whose opinion the unnamed line of the משנה follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה limits where one may rent houses to a גוי. רבי יוסי allows it everywhere, even in ארץ ישראל, so the משנה cannot be his view. It must follow רבי מאיר, who is stricter.

keyTerms.meaning: An unnamed, anonymous ruling in the משנה

phrases.english: And the unattributed ruling is like Rabbi Meir,
for if it were Rabbi Yosei,
in every place one may rent out.
phrases.notes: He means renting houses to a גוי, even in ארץ ישראל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the discussion from the previous part of the daf about renting houses.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The anonymous משנה about renting houses follows רבי מאיר, since רבי יוסי permits renting houses everywhere.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה on renting a bathhouse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: in every place, one may not rent out his bathhouse to a גוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: "And in every place, one may not rent out..." and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line of the משנה. This sets up the next discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the משנה was talking about rules that change from place to place. This line gives a rule that applies everywhere: a bathhouse may never be rented to a גוי.

keyTerms.meaning: Etc., and so on (the rest of the quote)

phrases.english: And in every place one may not rent out, etc.
phrases.notes: The "etc." points to the rest of the משנה: one may not rent out his bathhouse, because it's called by the owner's name.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may never rent out a bathhouse to a גוי, in any place.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל explains the reason
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. The bathhouse is called by the owner's name, so the גוי's work there on שבת and יום טוב looks like the Jew's work.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: A person may not rent out his bathhouse to a גוי. It is called by the owner's name, and this גוי works in it on שבת and יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that spells out why the משנה forbids renting out a bathhouse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem is not the גוי's work itself. People know the bathhouse as the Jew's, so they will think the Jew is having it run for him on שבת and יום טוב. This one reason will be the basis for both inferences that come next.

keyTerms.meaning: It is called by his (the owner's) name

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: It was taught: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
A person may not rent out his bathhouse to a gentile,
because it is called by his name,
and this gentile does work in it
on Shabbatot and on Festivals.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind the משנה quoted in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A bathhouse may not be rented to a גוי, because it carries the owner's name and the גוי works it on שבת and יום טוב.
steps.whyThisMatters: The whole rest of the section measures every other case against this one reason.

steps.title: What about renting to a כותי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about renting a bathhouse to a כותי. It infers that this is allowed, since only a גוי is mentioned.
steps.simpleTranslation: But to a כותי, what is the law? It is allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא infers from the ברייתא that renting a bathhouse to a כותי is permitted. It sets up a challenge to that inference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא forbids renting only to a גוי, because he works on שבת and יום טוב. Since a כותי is not mentioned, the גמרא concludes that renting to him is fine.

phrases.english: But to a Samaritan, what?
It is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the ברייתא in step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether renting a bathhouse to a כותי is also forbidden.

steps.title: But the כותי might work there on חול המועד
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: a כותי might work in the bathhouse on חול המועד, so why is it permitted?
steps.simpleTranslation: But say the כותי will do work in it during חול המועד!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on allowing a כותי. He might run the bathhouse on חול המועד, which would look bad for the Jewish owner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry from step 3 was that the owner would be suspected of having work done on holy days. The גמרא only raises חול המועד here, suggesting that a כותי would not work on שבת or יום טוב. So the question is whether חול המועד work should be a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: חול המועד, the intermediate days of a Festival

phrases.english: A Samaritan, say he does work in it
during the intermediate days of a Festival!

steps.triggerLanguage: כּוּתִי אֵימַר עָבֵיד בֵּיהּ מְלָאכָה בְּחוּלּוֹ שֶׁל מוֹעֵד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the permission given in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that renting a bathhouse to a כותי is permitted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A כותי may work the bathhouse on חול המועד, which could also make people suspect the Jewish owner.

steps.title: Jews also run bathhouses on חול המועד
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that on חול המועד Jews themselves work and run bathhouses, so there is nothing to suspect.
steps.simpleTranslation: On חול המועד, we also do that work.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge: running a bathhouse on חול המועד is allowed even for Jews.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The concern is only that people will think the owner is doing something forbidden. Since Jews may heat bathhouses on חול המועד, nothing looks wrong, and renting to a כותי stays permitted.

phrases.english: During the intermediate days of a Festival
we too do work.
phrases.notes: He means Jews also heat and run bathhouses then.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּחוּלּוֹ שֶׁל מוֹעֵד אֲנַן נָמֵי עָבְדִינַן
steps.terutzResolutionType: Removes the concern: the activity is not forbidden for Jews either.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Work done by a כותי on חול המועד would cast suspicion on the Jewish owner.
steps.terutzMaskana: Jews also work bathhouses on חול המועד, so renting to a כותי is permitted.

steps.title: What about renting a field to a גוי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers that renting out a field to a גוי is permitted, since only a bathhouse is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: But his field to a גוי, what is the law? It is allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a second inference from the ruling: a field may be rented to a גוי. This sets up the reason and a challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A field is also known by its owner's name, and a גוי would also work it on שבת. Even so, the ruling singles out only a bathhouse, so a field must be permitted.

phrases.english: But his field to a gentile, what?
It is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second inference from the ruling in step 3, parallel to step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether renting a field to a גוי is forbidden like a bathhouse.

steps.title: A sharecropper works for his own share
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why a field is permitted: everyone knows a sharecropper works the field for his own share.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? A sharecropper works for his own sharecropping.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason a field is different from a bathhouse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sharecropping fields is common, so people seeing a גוי work a Jew's field on שבת assume he is working for his own share. Nobody thinks the Jew hired him, so there is no suspicion.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
A sharecropper works for his own sharecropping.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the permission given in step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a field may be rented to a גוי.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: People assume a sharecropper works for his own share, not for the Jewish owner.

steps.title: Why not say the same about a bathhouse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: people should also assume the גוי running a bathhouse is a sharecropper working for himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: For a bathhouse too, let us say: the sharecropper works for his own sharecropping!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the sharecropper reasoning doesn't permit renting out a bathhouse too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the field is allowed because people assume the גוי works for himself, the same logic seems to fit a bathhouse. That would undo the משנה's ban.

phrases.english: A bathhouse too, let them say:
the sharecropper works for his own sharecropping?

steps.triggerLanguage: מֶרְחָץ נָמֵי אָמְרִי: אֲרִיסָא אֲרִיסוּתֵיהּ קָעָבֵיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the reason from step 8 to attack the ban on bathhouses from step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The prohibition against renting a bathhouse to a גוי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The sharecropper reasoning that permits a field should permit a bathhouse as well.

steps.title: Nobody sharecrops a bathhouse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that people do not usually run a bathhouse as sharecroppers, so onlookers will assume the גוי is the Jew's hired worker.
steps.simpleTranslation: People do not usually make sharecropping arrangements for a bathhouse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the sharecropper idea doesn't apply, because bathhouses are not normally run that way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What people suspect depends on what is common. Sharecropping a field is normal, so no one suspects the owner. Sharecropping a bathhouse is not normal, so people will think the גוי is working for the Jew, and the ban stays.
steps.whatToRemember: A bathhouse may not be rented to a גוי because it carries the owner's name and people will think the Jew is having it run on שבת. A כותי is allowed, since on חול המועד Jews run bathhouses too. A field is allowed, since sharecropping a field is common and a bathhouse is not.
steps.confusionAlert: The problem is not the work itself. It is what onlookers will think about the Jewish owner, which is why the outcome depends on what is normal practice.

phrases.english: A sharecropper of a bathhouse
people do not make.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the cases based on common practice.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: People would assume a גוי running a bathhouse is a sharecropper, just as with a field.
steps.terutzMaskana: Bathhouses are not sharecropped, so people would assume the גוי works for the Jew, and the ban remains.

steps.title: Do not rent a field to a כותי
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר rules that a Jew may not rent his field to a כותי, because the field is known as the Jew's and the כותי will work it on חול המועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: A person should not rent out his field to a כותי (a Samaritan). The field is known by the owner's name, and this כותי will work it on חול המועד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source, a ברייתא, about renting a field to a כותי. It sounds very close to the bathhouse discussion we just finished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is about how it looks. People know the field as the Jew's field. When they see someone working it on חול המועד, they might think the Jew is having his own work done on חול המועד.

keyTerms.meaning: A Samaritan (a member of the כותים)
It is called by his name, meaning people know it as his field
חול המועד, the middle days of a festival, when some work is forbidden

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
A person may not rent out his field to a Samaritan,
because it is called by his name,
phrases.notes: "His name" means the Jewish owner's name. Everyone knows it as his field.

phrases.english: and this Samaritan does work in it
on the intermediate days of the festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a parallel source about a field. It matches the earlier bathhouse and field reasoning (Steps 3-10).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Do not rent your field to a כותי, because it is known as your field and he will work it on חול המועד.

steps.title: So renting to a גוי is permitted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers from the ברייתא that renting a field to a גוי is permitted, because people assume a sharecropper works for his own share.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about a גוי? It is permitted, because people say: the אריס (sharecropper) is working for his own share.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the ברייתא closely. Since it only forbids a כותי, it must allow a גוי, and the גמרא explains why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Onlookers who see a גוי working the field assume he is an אריס working for his own cut of the crop, not for the Jew. So the suspicion that the Jew is having his work done does not come up. This is the same reasoning used for a field in Step 8.

keyTerms.meaning: Because people say (this is what onlookers assume)
A sharecropper, who works a field in return for a share of the crop
He is doing his own sharecropping, meaning he works for his own share

phrases.english: But a gentile, what is the law?
It is permitted,
since people say: the sharecropper is working for his own share.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a conclusion from what the ברייתא in Step 11 leaves out.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Since the ברייתא only forbids a כותי, what is the law for a גוי?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is permitted, because people assume a sharecropper works for himself.

steps.title: Why not say the same about a כותי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: if people assume a גוי sharecropper works for himself, they should assume the same about a כותי.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, about a כותי people should also say: the אריס is working for his own share!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the difference between a גוי and a כותי. The reason given for allowing a גוי seems to fit a כותי just as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 permitted a גוי because onlookers assume an אריס works for his own share. Nothing in that reason depends on who the worker is, so the same assumption should cover a כותי. Then why does רבי שמעון בן אלעזר forbid renting to a כותי?

keyTerms.meaning: If so, a standard way to open a challenge

phrases.english: If so,
about a Samaritan too, people would say:
the sharecropper is working for his own share!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the reason from Step 12 to challenge the ruling of Step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's ruling that renting to a כותי is forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The sharecropper reason that allows a גוי should apply equally to a כותי, so there seems to be no reason to forbid it.
